objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A southern Thai prayer hall inside a walled compound. A whitewashed courtyard wall with a proud coping and a flat-topped gate block carrying a raised border and a Moorish doorway; a white hall 11.0 x 9.9 x 5.46 m whose front is an open five-bay Moorish loggia -- three doorways between two blind niches on a pale green field -- under a cornice ledge, a parapet with a green band and a white coping; a square podium and a round drum with twelve pointed windows carrying the great ribbed dome and its gilt crescent; four small ribbed domes on ringed drums at the roof corners; and a square tapering minaret engaged with the left wall, with a corbelled octagonal balcony, an eight-arch lantern, a ribbed dome and a crescent.

reasoning: The registry notes name the recognisable pairing exactly -- ONE large ribbed dome plus a single slender minaret -- and the proxy places the minaret ENGAGED with the hall's left wall rather than free-standing in the courtyard, which is where the first build put it.
Six ribbed domes across three systems, a five-bay Moorish loggia with three real openings, a twelve-window drum, an eight-arch minaret lantern, and a walled courtyard with a gate.
Four materials carry weathering as post-construction canvas tiles; the dome carries two measured colours through per-vertex rib striping.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The loggia is a REAL recess: the arched screen wall stands 1.8 m in front of the pale green inner wall, roofed by the same slab, so the three doorways read as openings from every azimuth rather than as dark panels painted on a solid block.

silhouette.description: A low walled compound to 1.65 m, a wide low hall to 5.46 m, a drum and a ribbed dome to 9.50 m with a gilt cap, ball, spike and crescent to 10.85 m, four small domes at the roof corners to 7.55 m, and an engaged minaret to 12.00 m. The silhouette events are the great dome, the minaret, the loggia rhythm and the corner-dome cluster.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -7.05..+7.05 and z spans -8.05..+8.05, the courtyard wall plus its 5 cm coping on the declared 14 x 16 footprint. y spans 0.00 to 11.998, the top of the MINARET's crescent. The height is the SECOND BUILD's correction: the first shipped 18 m on the registry notes' word alone, and the Meshy proxy read with scratch/_mon/vox.mjs and front.mjs spans 1.77 x 1.90 units in plan against 1.447 tall, so at 14 x 16 m the compound is 11.6-12.3 m high (mean 12.0). The declaration was corrected to 12 m with that arithmetic in the registry notes before this build, and every height here is a row of the proxy depth maps at 69.75 px/m: hall parapet 5.46 (row 456), dome crown 9.50 (row 175), corner domes 7.18 (row 336), minaret balcony 9.10 (side map row 190).
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate, compared band by band with scratch/_mon/bands.mjs (area-weighted surface sampling, 5-95 pct width and depth per tenth of height): mean |delta width| 0.026 and |delta depth| 0.032 of height, against 0.300 / 0.243 for the first build. Bands 2-9 agree within 0.036 on width; the two residuals are band 0, where the candidate reads 1.097 against 1.206 because the thin courtyard wall carries little of the sampled surface and the 95th percentile falls inside it, and band 7-8 depth (+0.07 / +0.04) where the minaret lantern and the dome ornament span slightly more z than the proxy's.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.65: the compound is bilaterally symmetric and the domes are surfaces of revolution, but the LOGGIA is on one elevation only and the minaret is on one side, so the rear and the right side are authored as plain streaked render, which is what the proxy's -Z and +X depth maps show.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. materials.note: white covers the courtyard wall, the hall, the arcade surrounds, the drum, the corner drums AND the minaret -- six consumers, one render. uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 17,088 of 32,000, and nearly all of it is domes: six ribbed surfaces at 96, 64 and 48 radial samples. That is the correct place to spend it -- the ribs are what make a dome a mosque dome at the distance a village skyline is read from -- and the draw-call axis is at half its ceiling.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Ribbed surfaces of revolution, Moorish-arch extrusions with holes, an extruded U plan, octagonal prisms, a lathe ring, a flat crescent extrusion and boxes. The arched screen wall is ONE extrusion of a rectangle carrying three arch holes, which is what makes the loggia a real recess at no extra draw call.

Three InstancedMesh systems carry 11 of the prop's discrete parts. The corner domes carry their rib striping through the same per-vertex attribute as the great dome, so instancing costs the stripe nothing.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Three seeded Canvas 2D tiles -- render, pale green and screed -- are bound as map and bumpMap AFTER construction, in multiplier space over white, with v keyed to the top of each part so the mould band and drips hang from every coping; under Node there is no canvas and the materials render their flat measured colour.
